title: Break an ownership cycle with a weak parent link
prompt: A parent owns each child through children. A child remembers its parent without owning it. makeChild registers one child and returns it. When the last external parent owner goes away, both objects must be destroyable.
signature: struct Node: weak_ptr<Node> parent; vector<shared_ptr<Node>> children; makeChild(shared_ptr<Node>)

tests.label: Parent visible
tests.hint: A weak parent link can be locked while parent exists.

tests.label: Cycle releases
tests.hint: Do not have child keep its parent alive.

tests.label: Child survives alone
tests.hint: A live child must notice a departed parent.

hints: shared_ptr adds ownership; weak_ptr observes without adding ownership.
The parent’s vector owns children; children should not own their parent.
explanation: A strong cycle cannot reach an owner count of zero by itself. A weak back-reference breaks that cycle while allowing a checked lock() when the parent still exists.
